articles.title: ‘We are the reason that data centers get built and expanded’: It’s not about whether we need them, but it’s about where we build them, IDCA founder and CEO says
articles.content: Adding to the existing pressures that data centers face regarding energy supply and grid connections, land shortages and chip availability, many hyperscalers are now facing local opposition to project proposals. At a congressional hearing earlier this year, US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez presented two jars of murky water, filled from homes in Morgan County, Georgia, near one of Meta’s data center campuses. Though Meta has disputed any connection between its construction work and residents’ private wells and water sources, tensions are becoming harder to ignore as the digital world’s physical infrastructure continues to expand. We are creating our own data center paradox Enterprise demand for cloud compute and the mass consumer and enterprise consumption of AI have ultimately led to a surge in demand for physical data centers, but they’re now being seen in a similar vein to airports and power stations – physical infrastructure that’s used by nearly all citizens, but projects that nobody actually wants to live by. And it’s this paradox that many are grappling with at the moment – in this case, residents with a Facebook account can hardly argue against Meta’s need for physical infrastructure, and the same logic applies to users of streaming platforms, ecommerce websites, cloud storage, AI chatbots and so much more. While International Data Center Authority (IDCA) founder and CEO Mehdi Paryavi believes this digital hypocrisy could afford hyperscalers some justification in their actions, it’s clear that service providers and infrastructure companies are not valuing communication and public engagement enough. With hyperscalers planning data center buildouts years in advance and chipmakers facing major backlogs, it’s no longer about whether we need extra capacity – rather, it’s about where that compute should reside and how communities are consulted and engaged. Should data centres be renamed as data factories instead given that they essentially process data at scale? Data centers are just fine with their current naming. Data centers come in different sizes and types, fulfilling diverse purposes. Some produce data and house AI as AI factories, some import and house data from the cloud and enterprise applications, some just serve as internet exchange and telecom shelter, and some just sit on your desk as USB drives and PCs that just house data with the least amenities. Data centers are more holistic and overarching than data factories, while the latter is easier to understand for the general public. What differentiates data centers from one another is not their sheer size, but rather the type of data they house or process. Depending on the use case, a small enterprise data center that is home to very sensitive information might prove to be more mission-critical than a large-scale AI data center that manufactures data at scale. You mention that if you have a Facebook account, you can’t complain about data centers. I assume that this rings true for all hyperscalers and big cloud services as well. Is there any going back and what can be done to educate users more? Our Facebook account, Amazon shopping cart, Gmail, iMessage or WhatsApp, Netflix, online banking, Google Maps, YouTube, ChatGPT, will simply cease to exist without data centers. We are the reason that data centers get built and expanded. Our “consumption” and demand for higher speeds and better quality of service in the utilization of AI and Cloud services and the technological amenities we receive on an ever-evolving and ever-growing basis draw data centers to our communities. Speaking of consumers, on the subject of it being digital hypocrisy to describe the paradoxical relationship between the user and the service provider. Can you expand on that further? When you protest against the expansion of data centers, yet you publicize your protest on social media that are solely enabled through data centers, when you oppose the development of data centers while they…

articles.summaryFa: مدیرعامل IDCA بر تمرکز بر مکان ساخت مراکز داده تأکید می‌کند و نگران مخالفت‌های محلی و چالش‌های زیرساختی است. او معتقد است باید به جای تمرکز صرف روی توسعه، در مورد مکان و تعامل با جامعه‌ها فکر کنیم. این نگرانی‌ها در حالی است که تقاضا برای زیرساخت‌های فیزیکی از جمله مراکز داده در حال افزایش است.
articles.summaryEn: IDCA CEO emphasizes the importance of location and community engagement in data center development amid rising local opposition and infrastructure challenges. The surge in demand for data centers is now about choosing the right places and better stakeholder communication.

articles.whyItMattersFa: این خبر اهمیت دارد چون آینده توسعه زیرساخت‌های فناوری اطلاعات و نحوه تعامل با جوامع را مشخص می‌کند و بر سیاست‌گذاری‌های مسئولانه در حوزه فناوری تأثیر می‌گذارد.
